title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Holiday: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted historical lift: x1.49 (2 past occurrences); consistent with past 3 years.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.1. Thanksgiving historically lifts sales to x1.49 vs baseline (noise-adjusted), supported by two past occurrences. The price increase to $5.72 (+3.4%) is modest and not likely to offset demand, especially with a new competitor opening across the street, which may draw customers. The classical uplift model suggests x1.49, but this is already based on the same noise-adjusted event effect. No promotion is planned, and the post-promo dip is not triggered. The competitor entry adds downside risk, but no data shows its impact on this product. We retain the event lift but shrink slightly due to uncertain competitive impact and thin evidence. No other drivers are active.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-29 (7 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Thanksgiving (Thu)
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.9 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
